correctness.rationale: The exact ground-state Gram sum proves positivity and simple bottom eigenvalue; the sine-boundary recurrence and explicitly simplified finite trigonometric sums make the top-singular directional derivative vanish. A fixed top singular vector gives the exact strict squared-norm increase for all other complex scalars. The calibrated singular pair, support bound, strict q-monotonicity and disk von Neumann criterion prove the full iff spectral-set statement. All n are proved analytically; exact and numeric finite checks were separately run on the actual bundled script.

originality.rationale: The exact unrestricted complex minimizing coefficient and the sharp dimension-by-dimension 1-spectral threshold were not contained in the inspected full primary texts. The 2007 exact same one-step Jordan minimization is explicitly bounded rather than solved. The 2026 universal scaled-q constant implies only the dimension-free 4/5 sufficient cutoff, not the larger threshold here. An implicit prior q-radius envelope requires a nontrivial separate spectral optimization and does not explicitly identify the unique complex pencil minimizer. Residual risk remains from unindexed exact scalar optimization and inaccessible full texts.
residual_risks: The primary full texts of arXiv:2608.09866 and arXiv:2610.00443 were inaccessible, so an internal example not visible in their abstracts may overlap.
A differently named older operator-norm minimization formula might imply the all-dimensional scalar coefficient.
The known Jordan q-radius implicit envelope is close in object and may be viewed as an implicit determination of the cutoff, although it does not state the exact unique complex minimizer.

value.rationale: The paper provides the all-n unique complex scalar exactly for a canonically motivated one-step operator-norm approximation. This fills a genuine published two-sided cosine-bound gap in the 2007 Jordan GMRES literature and upgrades the new scaled-q spectral-set theory from a universal sufficient 4/5 to sharp operator-specific thresholds approaching 1. The full optimizer and strict complex uniqueness require a structural trigonometric eigenspace identity; the claim is neither a finite-table recomputation nor a parameter renaming.
